messages.subject: RE: [R-sig-teaching] FW: Deducer 0.1 Released
parts:
Graham,

Thank you for the comments. Indeed the top two items on my to do list are
plots and a plug-in architecture, so plotting will be gotten too soon. In
the mean time, you can get some visualizations from the plot buttons in the
analysis dialogs.

Regarding output tables... I have tried to redo the printing of results so
that the output is in nice tables. Take for example doing a one-way anova on
4 variables. Deducer outputs:

-- Deducer Command --
k.sample.test(variables=c(X1,X2,X3,X4),
factor.var=fact1,
data=test.data,
test=oneway.test)
-- End Command --
One-way analysis of means (not assuming equal
variances)
F (num df,denom df) p-value
X1 0.4186999 (5,37.89) 0.83275569
X2 0.3508936 (5,33.746) 0.87804437
X3 2.9354098 (5,35.299) 0.02561935
X4 1.2085369 (5,36.631) 0.32456574

Compare this to the normal output given by R. This is especially apparent in
the implementation of contingency tables.

Cheers,
Ian

R output without Deducer:

> oneway.test(X1~fact1,data=test.data)

One-way analysis of means (not assuming equal variances)

data: X1 and fact1
F = 0.4187, num df = 5.00, denom df = 37.89, p-value = 0.8328

> oneway.test(X2~fact1,data=test.data)

One-way analysis of means (not assuming equal variances)

data: X2 and fact1
F = 0.3509, num df = 5.000, denom df = 33.746, p-value = 0.878

> oneway.test(X3~fact1,data=test.data)

One-way analysis of means (not assuming equal variances)

data: X3 and fact1
F = 2.9354, num df = 5.000, denom df = 35.299, p-value = 0.02562

> oneway.test(X4~fact1,data=test.data)

One-way analysis of means (not assuming equal variances)

data: X4 and fact1
F = 1.2085, num df = 5.000, denom df = 36.631, p-value = 0.3246

-----Original Message-----
From: Graham Smith [mailto:myot...@gmail.com]

To: Fellows, Ian
Subject: Re: [R-sig-teaching] FW: Deducer 0.1 Released

Ian,

I teach introductory statistics using R at Bath Spa University. You
will possibly have seen some of my comments and questions elsewhere on
the r-sig-teaching list.

Worth noting is that I only teach in terms of producing results to go
into scientific papers or technical reports so I am especially
interested in making good quality output easier.

I have just installed on Ubuntu to try this out. I am not familiar
with JGR so this is also new.

My first impressions are that it is better than RCmdr in that it
allows a more direct interaction with the command line while still
giving a menu option if you get stuck. The print out of the commands
that can be accessed and edited as a normal command line (via history)
is very useful.

Although, I introduce students to RCmdr, I still teach the command
line. Deducer seems to offer a better compromise.

My negative comments in terms of features, which is a bit unfair as
its just 0.1, is that menu access to plotting would be useful, as I
instruct my students not to do anything until after having had a look
at their data with scatter plots and box plots, etc.

Indeed graphics are a tad tedious, so a gui that allowed adding
titles. labels etc would be welcomed.

Second problem students have is presenting tables so outputting tables
of results in a presentation style quality would be nice.

Thirdly, negative binomial on the GLM menu would also be nice, I know
it isn't strictly part of the GLM family, but teaching ecologists
where count data with lots of zeros is very common, this is an
important distribution. Also for ecologists, menu access to Vegan and
violin plots would also be extremely useful, but I appreciate this is
a bit too specialist for the majority. However, customisation for
specific disciplines (based on the R task views) would make it an
especially attractive option

I am currently trying to put together a Virtual Machine to distribute
to students based on http://www.gisvm.com/

and part of this will be to add something like Deducer before I
distribute my modified version of GISVM.

I hope you get some support for this, as it seems a worthwhile
addition to the R GUIs.

Graham

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
>
>
> Deducer 0.1 has been released to CRAN
>
> Deducer is designed to be a free, easy to use, alternative to proprietary
> software such as SPSS, JMP, and Minitab. It has a menu system to do common
> data manipulation and data analysis tasks, and an excel-like spreadsheet
in
> which to view and edit data frames. The goal of the project is to two
fold.
>
>        1. Provide an intuitive interface so that non-technical users
>           can learn and perform analyses without programming getting
>           in their way.
>        2. Increase the efficiency of expert R users when performing
>         common tasks by replacing hundreds of keystrokes with a few
>         mouse clicks. Also, as much as possible the GUI should not
>         get in their way if they just want to do some programming.
>
> Deducer is integrated into the Windows RGui, and the cross-platform Java
> console JGR, and is also usable and accessible from the command line.
> Screen shots and examples can be viewed in the online wiki manual:
>
> http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.DeducerManual
>
> Comments and questions are more than welcome. A discussion group has been
> created for any questions or recommendations.
>
> http://groups.google.com/group/deducer
>
> Deducer Features:
>
> Data manipulation:
>        1. Factor editor
>        2. Variable recoding
>        3. data sorting
>        4. data frame merging
>        5. transposing a data frame
>        6. subseting
>
> Analysis:
>        1. Frequencies
>        2. Descriptives
>        3. Contingency tables
>                a. Nicely formatted tables with optional
>                        i. Percentages
>                        ii. Expected counts
>                        iii. Residuals
>                b. Statistical tests
>                        i. chi-squared
>                        ii. likelihood ratio
>                        iii. fisher's exact
>                        iv. mantel haenszel
